claims.text: Local enrichment of Cu at the surface governs the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Surface enrichment of Cu induces surface premelting that subsequently triggers bulk melting.
The starting nanoparticles are homogeneous random solid solutions with uniform elemental distributions.
A mild annealing treatment in reducing H2/Ar can promote surface segregation of Cu relative to an untreated baseline.
The relevant premelting-to-melting regime is approximately 800–1300 K.
A hold near 1000 K for approximately 30 minutes allows surface evolution.
Localized aggregation of Cu at the nanoparticle surface lowers the local melting threshold.
The lowered local melting threshold produces a thin liquid-like surface layer.
The liquid-like surface layer facilitates eventual full-particle melting.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other relevant components and therefore creates surface regions with reduced melting temperatures when it segregates.
Liquid-like surface zones act as nucleation sites for bulk melting.
Nanoparticles with enhanced surface Cu segregation will show an earlier melting onset than initially uniform nanoparticles.
The earlier melting onset will appear as a distinct lower-temperature endothermic DSC signal.
Nanoparticles with enhanced surface Cu segregation will progress to full melting more rapidly than the baseline particles.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to nanoparticles with high surface-to-volume ratios.
The proposed mechanism may not apply directly to bulk materials, large nanoparticles with minimized surface effects, or oxidized nanoparticle surfaces.
Particle-size distribution, minor oxide formation, and other segregation phenomena may affect the transition-temperature shift and melting kinetics.
Failure of the Cu-enriched particles to exhibit a statistically significant earlier premelting onset than the untreated baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
